newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybean gains slashed on USDA export figures.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybean gains slashed on USDA export figures.

text.p: Gains in CBOT old crop soybean futures were slashed within seconds of the release of USDA's weekly export inspections data which came in below trade expectations, floor sources said.
Trade sources had expected the weekly figure to show between 10 million and 14 million bushels of soybeans inspected for export. The actual figure was 5.988 million bushels.
The figure suggested prices had risen enough to temper demand for U.S. supplies. USDA in April forecast U.S. ending soybean stocks would total 125 million bushels, the lowest in 20 years.

Earlier on Monday and ahead of the USDA export inspections report, the May contract topped $9.00 per bushel for the first time since the 1988 drought. Contract highs also were notched in the May and July on concerns the weekly export tally would show demand remained strong.
At 1006 CDT, soybeans were down 2-1/2 cents per bushel to up four with July down 2-1/2 at $8.83.
